voyage: Battery C's embarkation roster of 17 Jul (p0561-p0564). The report of 18 Jul has the battery aboard; on 19 Jul it is at Gela, a week after the first landings there (10 Jul).
about: A US Navy tank landing ship (LST-1 class), built by Bethlehem Steel at Quincy, Mass., and commissioned on 23 Jan 1943. She took part in the Sicily landings (July 1943), Salerno (September 1943) and Normandy (June 1944), and earned three battle stars. Scrapped 1947.

voyage: 9 Aug 1944, 1200: "4 Officers, 87 EM Boarded LST 318, 2 Officer 31 EM Boarded LST 313" in Naples harbour (p1143). 12 Aug: "1630 hrs left Naples Harbor, Mission Unknown" (p1146). 15 Aug: landed near Sainte-Maxime; the battalion's first tracks were on the beach at about 1030 and everything was ashore by 1400 (battalion history, ok45th-17564/p05). Most of the forward detachment was on 318.
about: Not the US Navy's LST-318, which was sunk by German aircraft off Caronia, Sicily, on 9 Aug 1943. The number the clerk typed (twice, on 9 and 12 Aug) may be a serial in the landing's loading plan rather than a hull number, or mistyped. Which ship it was isn't known.

voyage: 2 officers and 31 men of the forward detachment boarded "LST 313" (p1143).
about: Not the US Navy's LST-313, which was sunk by German aircraft off Gela on 10 Jul 1943. As with 318, the number may be a loading serial or mistyped; the ship isn't known.

voyage: 16 Oct 1943: the detachment's station is "Ship # 416" (p0622), after the Bizerte staging area, its station since 1 Oct. 17 Oct: Agnano racecourse, Naples (p0624).
about: The report gives no type. One candidate is HM LST-416, an American-built tank landing ship (Bethlehem-Fairfield, Baltimore) commissioned into the Royal Navy on 3 Feb 1943, but no source found puts her on the Bizerte-Naples run that October. Unconfirmed.

voyage: 1 Sep 1944: "Two Officers & 5 EM Relvd Fr rations Hq & Hq Btry to Det for rations to the U.S.S. Florence Nightingale (1230)" (p0668). By 4 Sep the detachment was ashore at Cogolin. Its last station before was Qualiano, near Naples (21 Aug); the navy history describes her reinforcement voyages to southern France as from Oran, so where she took the detachment aboard isn't settled.
about: A US Navy transport (Elizabeth C. Stanton class), launched in 1940 at Oakland, Calif., as the freighter Mormacsun; 492 ft, 18 knots. She landed troops at Port Lyautey, Morocco (Nov 1942) and Scoglitti, Sicily (Jul 1943), sortied from Naples for the 15 Aug 1944 assault on southern France, and carried reinforcements there until 25 Oct. Later in the Pacific (Okinawa, May 1945). Four battle stars.
